prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- Police are searching for any other alleged victims of a Sunday school teacher accused of raping and killing an 8-year-old girl from Tracy, California. Melissa Huckaby is charged with killing 8-year-old Sandra Cantu, who was a friend of her own daughter. "We are asking the public if they have any indication that any of their children may have had inappropriate contact with [the suspect] to contact us," Tracy Police Sgt. Tony Sheneman said Tuesday evening. "There has been no indication that this has happened. But she is a Sunday school teacher and did have contact with children, so that is why we are asking." Melissa Huckaby, 28, was arrested and charged with killing and raping 8-year-old Sandra Cantu, a friend of her 5-year-old daughter. Huckaby, wearing red jail scrubs over a white T-shirt, was in court Tuesday for an arraignment. She was charged with murder, kidnapping, the performance of a lewd and lascivious act on a child under 14 and rape by instrument. If convicted, Huckaby would face the death penalty or life in prison without parole, San Joaquin County District Attorney James Willett told reporters after the hearing. A decision on whether to seek the death penalty will be made later, he said. Huckaby did not enter a plea or speak during the court hearing, although she flinched when Sandra Cantu's name was spoken, and she cried at times. Sandra's body was found April 6, stuffed into a suitcase and submerged in a pond at a dairy farm. Huckaby was arrested Friday night after questioning by police. Sandra was last seen alive March 27 in the mobile home park where she lived with her family -- the same mobile home park where Huckaby lives with her daughter. The two children were close friends and played together frequently, police said. Huckaby is the granddaughter of Clifford Lane Lawless, pastor of Clover Road Baptist Church near the mobile home park, and she taught Sunday school at the church, police have said. The church was searched as part of the investigation into Sandra's disappearance and death. Before her arrest, Huckaby acknowledged to a newspaper reporter that she owned the suitcase that contained Sandra's body. But Huckaby said the suitcase had been stolen. Willett declined to comment on any of the evidence or allegations in the case, saying evidence would be presented in court. A memorial ceremony is scheduled for Sandra at 1 p.m. Thursday at a high school in Tracy, police said. -- CNN's Ninette Sosa contributed to this report.

# Melissa Huckaby Arraigned in Killing of 8-Year-Old Sandra Cantu; Death Penalty Possible

**TRACY, Calif. —** Melissa Huckaby, the California Sunday school teacher accused of kidnapping, sexually assaulting and killing 8-year-old Sandra Cantu, appeared in court to face charges that could make her eligible for the death penalty.

Huckaby, 28, was arraigned in San Joaquin County on a murder charge accompanied by special-circumstance allegations, including that the killing occurred during a kidnapping and sexual assault. Prosecutors also alleged lewd or lascivious conduct involving a child.

She did not enter a plea during the brief proceeding, and the case was continued to allow her defense attorney additional time. Huckaby remained jailed without bail.

The special-circumstance allegations make the case eligible for capital punishment under California law. Prosecutors said, however, that no final decision had been made on whether to seek the death penalty. Such a decision would be made by the San Joaquin County district attorney after reviewing the evidence and consulting Sandra’s family.

Huckaby is presumed innocent unless proved guilty.

## Child’s Body Found in Suitcase

Sandra disappeared from the Orchard Estates Mobile Home Park in Tracy on March 27, 2009. Surveillance video showed the second-grader walking near her home shortly before she vanished, prompting an intensive search involving police, federal agents, volunteers and residents.

Ten days later, farmworkers draining an irrigation pond several miles from the mobile-home park found Sandra’s body inside a suitcase. Authorities have not publicly disclosed all details of the evidence or the precise cause of death.

Huckaby lived in the same mobile-home park and was the granddaughter of a local pastor. She also taught Sunday school, a position that brought her into contact with children in the community. Investigators arrested her after questioning her and examining statements she had made about a missing suitcase.

## Police Ask Parents to Come Forward

As the criminal case moved into court, Tracy police issued an urgent appeal to parents whose children may have had contact with Huckaby through church, Sunday school, the mobile-home park or other activities.

Investigators asked families to report any unusual encounters, unexplained illnesses, gaps in memory, suspicious invitations, gifts or other behavior that might now appear significant. Police emphasized that the request did not mean they had identified additional victims, but said they needed to determine whether Huckaby had inappropriate contact with any other children.

Authorities urged parents not to conduct detailed interviews of their children themselves, warning that repeated or leading questions could frighten a child or complicate a later forensic interview. Instead, they asked parents with concerns to contact investigators so trained specialists could speak with the children.

The appeal widened the scope of the investigation beyond Sandra’s death and reflected concern about Huckaby’s access to children. Detectives were also reviewing her background, relationships and activities before her arrest.

The prosecution is expected to rely on forensic evidence, witness statements and evidence connected to the suitcase in which Sandra was found. Further details are likely to emerge as Huckaby enters a plea and the case advances toward a preliminary hearing.

# Suspect appears in court as police investigate California girl’s death

**TRACY, California (CNN) —** A woman accused of kidnapping and killing 8-year-old Sandra Cantu made a brief court appearance Tuesday as investigators continued examining evidence linking her to the suitcase in which the child’s body was found.

Melissa Huckaby, a 28-year-old Sunday school teacher and the mother of one of Sandra’s friends, did not enter a plea. Her arraignment on murder and kidnapping charges was postponed, and she remained in custody without bail.

Sandra disappeared March 27 from the mobile home park where she lived in Tracy, about 60 miles east of San Francisco. Ten days later, authorities recovered her body from an irrigation pond several miles away. She had been placed inside a suitcase.

The suitcase became a central piece of evidence in the investigation. Before her arrest, Huckaby told a local newspaper that a suitcase had been taken from her property around the time Sandra vanished. Police have said physical evidence connects Huckaby to the case but have released few details, citing the continuing investigation.

Authorities also searched Clover Road Baptist Church, where Huckaby taught Sunday school and her grandfather served as pastor. Investigators removed items from the church as well as from Huckaby’s home, though police have not publicly explained what was recovered or how it may relate to Sandra’s death.

Huckaby was arrested April 10 after hours of questioning. Prosecutors have alleged that Sandra was kidnapped and sexually assaulted before she was killed.

The case has shaken Tracy, where hundreds of volunteers helped search for the girl and distributed missing-person fliers.

A public memorial service for Sandra was planned for Thursday at Merrill F. West High School. Community members were expected to join her family in remembering the second-grader, whose disappearance and death drew national attention.
